$comment: Spelled-out Hinglish numbers for experience, lifted verbatim from signals.py.
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and must not be sorted: the alternation is built in this order, so
LONGEST-FIRST is what makes 'paune do' (1.75) win over 'paune' (0.75) and 'sava do' (2.25)
over 'sava' (1.25). The compounds mean different numbers; sorting this list silently
changes what a worker's answer means.
This is a PARITY fix, not a new inference: the table is the prompt's own table plus the
$comment_matcher: Capture group 1 is the QUANTITY — either digits or one of `wordNumbers`, spliced in by the
{EXP_WORDS} macro in file order so the longest compound wins.
The leading lookbehind rejects a quantity glued to a preceding digit or dot, so the '5' of
'12.5' or a part number cannot be read as an experience figure on its own.
The original used \d, which is Unicode-aware in Python and ASCII-only in JavaScript. Spelled
out as ASCII digits PLUS the Devanagari digit range so both engines agree. Note the UNIT
alternation is deliberately Latin-only, exactly as it shipped: '५ साल' does not match today and
this extraction does not change that. Widening it is a product decision, not a refactor.
